definitions.covered: Reviewed capability is implemented with source and behavioral-test evidence; not exhaustive differential conformance.
definitions.adapted: PHP provides the relevant capability through a different interface or an explicit supported execution model.
definitions.partial: Important behavior/configuration/typing is narrower; evidence documents current behavior, not the missing guarantee.
definitions.missing: No packaged equivalent; custom user code is not implementation parity.
definitions.excluded: Recommended deliberate non-goal, with PHP or legacy rationale.
definitions.extension: Beyond the baseline; excluded from parity assessment.

features.assessment: Exact/string/regex routing, multiple listeners, typed attributes and generic events work. Use message('', handler) or event('message', handler) for an unfiltered message listener.
Block/legacy selectors, first-action classification, regex constraints and submission-only view shorthand have explicit tests. view_closed is supported with explicit constraints.

Ordered synchronous middleware with short-circuiting and duplicate-next guards; listeners run sequentially and later listeners still run after earlier failures. No Promise scheduling parity is claimed.
Delivery exposes matches and per-constraint captures; HTTP and Socket Mode attach retry metadata. These are already implemented, not a missing Context feature.

Context is a delivery-local mutable capability shared across middleware, method/constructor-injected handlers and assistants in GenericContainer scopes. Separate deliveries/tenants/jobs get fresh contexts; the context is non-serializable and print_r/var_dump omit its values. Stock-adapter context factories remain separate.

Both stock transports expose typed input to a configured context factory after verification/authorization and before middleware. Factories enrich the existing fresh Context, cannot replace delivery authorization, and fail dispatch without an acknowledgement. HTTP headers/body and Socket Mode envelopes remain available; jobs retain only explicit inputs.
onlyEvents/onlyActions/etc and matchConstraints/message/command/event behavior live in typed registration and Matcher. Separate exported filter functions are unnecessary for this behavior.

MessageFilter.subtype() and MessageFilter.directMention() compose with ordinary middleware. Matching preserves raw text/captures, uses per-installation bot identity, follows leading-mention/whitespace behavior, and errors on missing bot identity without network lookups.
Static/custom authorization, tenant/user/enterprise identities, lifecycle exceptions and scoped clients work. User and bot grants remain separate.

App.verifyToken explicitly verifies and caches identity per App, hydrates both bot identifiers and checks verified tenant identity. auth:verify reports identity; socket:serve --verify-token hydrates the worker before connecting. SLACK_BOT_USER_ID/SLACK_BOT_ID support network-free HTTP. Help/discovery and ordinary dispatch do not perform hidden lookups; the CLI does not warm another process.

OAuth v2, bot/user scopes, one-time browser-bound state, denial handling, grant storage and OAuth callback endpoint handling are implemented. Opaque stored state deliberately replaces signed state-secret format.

Immutable InstallRequest supports per-flow bot/user scopes, workspace hints and server-side metadata. Atomic request/state consumption and per-flow cookies support concurrent tabs. Typed success/failure hooks run after the determined outcome, with persistence before success. Reusable OAuthHttpHandler supports host-owned paths and safe responses/redirects. Rendered installation pages remain host-owned; classic v1 and state-free installation flows remain deliberate exclusions.

Both grants refresh independently with locked updates, expiry windows and explicit long-lived-token migration. OAuth exchanges remain single-attempt. Store adapters carry update locking responsibility.
ConversationContext plus memory/file/SQLite stores implement read/update/expiry, with stronger installation scoping and explicit persistence rather than copying channel-only mutable JS state.
ThreadContext and durable adapters extend the Bolt baseline. Their presence is not evidence that unrelated Bolt features are implemented.

Reply provides channel/thread/ephemeral and response_url calls with typed messages. Helpers select explicit destinations; response URLs do not receive bot credentials. This replaces JS closures, not their names.

Typed return values produce one acknowledgement after inline processing. There is no early-ack callback, per-listener autoAcknowledge option or processBeforeResponse toggle. Named durable jobs are the supported slow-work path; a warning does not enforce Slack's deadline. Retain this PHP model and document the timing difference; any future async host needs a separate design.

features.area: Signed HTTP ingress and URL verification
features.assessment: Raw-body signature/timestamp checks, body limits, signed challenge, JSON/forms, retry headers and explicit error statuses are implemented. This does not include every configurable upstream receiver hook.

App.dispatch(body, metadata) already provides trusted parsed ingress, and Receiver.handle provides request/response verification. A new processEvent clone or generic receiver abstraction is not required. Future PSR/Laravel/Symfony adapters should reuse these methods.

features.area: Routes, ports, server lifecycle and initialization
features.assessment: Tempest owns HTTP routes and serving; SocketMode.Runner owns socket lifecycle. Custom routes can be normal Tempest controllers; relocating the supplied Slack/OAuth paths requires an application controller. No universal App.start/stop/init belongs in PHP-FPM.

App.onError receives original errors with listener/source/stage and buffered acknowledgement context; explicit Handled/Rethrow policy preserves originals, aggregates failures and cannot suppress failed authorization, durable intake or missing/duplicate acknowledgements. Legacy App.error remains. The HTTP receiver accepts non-success processing error responses; verification/rejection statuses and host route policy remain host-owned, with no early-ack/unhandled timer.
PSR-3 logger injection replaces @slack/logger, log-level enums and app.logger. Public logger property spelling is not required; normal Tempest logging configuration owns levels.

Envelope dispatch/ack payloads, hello/disconnect, health, bounds, reconnect/backoff and cooperative signal shutdown are implemented. No assertion of parity with every option in the separate Node Socket Mode SDK.

Legacy Assistant::make lifecycle, scoped thread context, status/title/prompts and streaming remain covered. Modern Agent View is opt-in and assessed separately as an extension, not baseline parity credit. Suggested prompts omit thread_ts in modern mode and retain it for legacy threads.

features.area: Custom function routing, inputs and terminal helpers
features.assessment: Named callbacks, strict typed inputs, function/interactivity execution context, workflow-scoped clients and complete/fail have behavioral tests. Execution guards duplicate and uncertain terminal calls per delivery; it does not promise global exactly-once completion across processes.

BoltConfig.attachFunctionToken defaults true, with an explicit false opt-out and strict SLACK_ATTACH_FUNCTION_TOKEN environment parsing. The selected workflow/bot/user client is consistent across injection, Reply and complete/fail. Authorizers still run; opting out requires installation credentials and never reuses a workflow-only grant as fallback.

features.area: Inbound native payload and state typing
features.assessment: Common event classes and native InputValue/FormState readers cover text, select and ID variants, radio/checkbox, date/time, files and rich text across actions and views. Raw access and existing value()/state() remain compatible. The complete @slack/types event universe and nested polymorphic data still have generic/raw fields; this is narrower native typing, not an unsupported routing family or a promise of one PHP DTO per TypeScript union. A later developer-experience slice adds typed App Home, channel lifecycle and message-metadata payloads, using a shared dispatch/validation/scaffolding catalog. Unknown events remain generic; the row stays partial for the wider event universe.

273 pinned/supplemental endpoint pairs and generic call(), uploads, pagination and explicit retries are implemented. A Web API transport audit is separate evidence; model coverage is not full Bolt runtime parity or coverage of every future Slack endpoint.

features.area: Express, Node server and AWS event classes
features.assessment: Do not port Express middleware, Node server objects, raw Node request/response buffers or Lambda callback/event types. A concrete PHP serverless adapter can be added if requested, reusing existing ingress.

features.area: JavaScript types, re-exports and coded-error names
features.assessment: Do not clone TypeScript utility types, Promise helpers, SDK/logger re-exports or each JS error class. PHP native types, exceptions, PSR interfaces and its package-owned SDK are the replacement. Behavioral errors remain in scope under errors/ack.

features.area: Unsigned production ingress and dev aliases
features.assessment: Keep signature verification mandatory in the signed HTTP receiver. Do not port an off switch merely for matching options. developerMode is a Node convenience preset; explicit PHP env/CLI configuration is sufficient.

The HTTP receiver returns empty 200 for an unambiguous top-level form ssl_check=1, discarding other fields without dispatch. Probes may be unsigned; normal delivery verification and body-size limits remain. Duplicate/array/lookalike probes are rejected and unsigned form inspection is bounded to 1,000 fields; PHP ends receipt directly rather than forwarding sanitized input.

features.area: Durable jobs, agent sessions and Work Objects
features.assessment: Named SQLite jobs, recovery/cancellation/retention, modern agent sessions and higher-level Work Object publishing are PHP product capabilities. They do not compensate for baseline gaps, and core function completion is only guarded per delivery.

features.area: Modern Agent View and typed streaming
features.assessment: Assistant::forAgentView routes human root DMs/replies and optional Messages-tab/focus events. Ordered app-context entities retain raw extensions and use fresh delivery scopes without stale focus fallback. Typed streaming values preserve raw arrays, bound whole-stream text/tasks and keep failures terminal. make:assistant --agent-view scaffolds modern handlers and Stop routing; the demo snapshots focus in a separate named SQLite job and reuses cancellable model execution. Live validation is recorded separately and does not broaden the pinned legacy Bolt baseline.

endpoints.assessment: Stock route is /slack/events; custom controller can call Receiver.handle. No endpoint-list config knob.

processBeforeResponse.assessment: Always process inline before response; explicit jobs replace slow inline work. No early-ack mode.

signatureVerification.assessment: Verification cannot be disabled on the signed HTTP receiver.

clientId.assessment: OAuthConfig and InstallationStore with installation-scoped grants.

clientSecret.assessment: OAuthConfig and InstallationStore with installation-scoped grants.

redirectUri.assessment: OAuthConfig and InstallationStore with installation-scoped grants.

scopes.assessment: OAuthConfig and InstallationStore with installation-scoped grants.

installationStore.assessment: OAuthConfig and InstallationStore with installation-scoped grants.

stateSecret.assessment: Opaque one-time state and browser binding replace signed state-secret encoding.

installerOptions.assessment: InstallRequest, atomic browser-bound state, typed hooks and reusable host-route handling cover the practical modern installation controls. Host pages, classic OAuth v1 and state-free direct installs are deliberate exclusions.

convoStore.assessment: ConversationStore adapter or false, with stronger key scoping.

token.assessment: BoltConfig token and Socket Mode Config appToken.

appToken.assessment: BoltConfig token and Socket Mode Config appToken.

botId.assessment: Static BoltConfig.botId, SLACK_BOT_ID and explicit verification hydration.

botUserId.assessment: Explicit BoltConfig value; no automatic token-only hydration.

receiver.assessment: Compose Receiver.handle and App.dispatch with the host.

ignoreSelf.assessment: Filters supplied or explicitly verified bot identity; no hidden boot/network lookup.

clientOptions.assessment: PSR-18 client plus explicit retry/upload configuration instead of Node options.

socketMode.assessment: Explicit socket:serve command and Socket Mode Config.

developerMode.assessment: No need for the Node convenience preset.

tokenVerificationEnabled.assessment: Explicit App.verifyToken, auth:verify and socket:serve --verify-token replace eager initialization.

deferInitialization.assessment: No equivalent async startup lifecycle to defer. Help/discovery need no token verification.

extendedErrorHandler.assessment: Typed App.onError(FailureContext):ErrorHandling plus safe HTTP processing-error response hook; legacy error callback retained.

attachFunctionToken.assessment: Default-on BoltConfig.attachFunctionToken and SLACK_ATTACH_FUNCTION_TOKEN; false selects authorized installation credentials.

client.assessment: Inject WebApi.Client or Delivery.client instead of reading App.client.

init.assessment: Host and runners own lifecycle; no Node server lifecycle clone. Explicit App::verifyToken() and socket:serve --verify-token provide identity verification without implicit discovery-time network calls.

start.assessment: Host and runners own lifecycle; no Node server lifecycle clone. Explicit App::verifyToken() and socket:serve --verify-token provide identity verification without implicit discovery-time network calls.

stop.assessment: Host and runners own lifecycle; no Node server lifecycle clone. Explicit App::verifyToken() and socket:serve --verify-token provide identity verification without implicit discovery-time network calls.

webClientOptions.assessment: Configure the PSR-18 transport and explicit retry policy.

use.assessment: Ordered pipeline with shared delivery-local Context.

function.assessment: Function routing, typed inputs, completion and token-attachment policy are implemented. PHP returned acknowledgements/named jobs replace explicit auto-ack callback/timing options.

event.assessment: Typed/fluent registration; unfiltered messages use an empty selector or event(message).

message.assessment: Typed/fluent registration; unfiltered messages use an empty selector or event(message).

command.assessment: Typed/fluent registration; unfiltered messages use an empty selector or event(message).

error.assessment: Legacy error callback remains; onError supplies typed delivery/stage/listener/ack context with explicit policy.

processEvent.assessment: Existing trusted App.dispatch replaces the Node ingress shape.
